en: Avoid perfume, heat and ultrasonic cleaners, since amber is a soft, organic stone that chemicals and vibration can damage. Wipe the ring gently with a soft cloth and store it apart from harder gemstones that could scratch it. Put the ring on last, after lotion and hairspray, and take it off before showering, swimming or sleeping. The 925 sterling silver setting darkens slowly with air; a soft silver cloth restores its shine. Cared for simply, an amber ring keeps its warm glow for decades.

en: Yes, every AMBERRA amber ring is set with genuine natural Baltic amber — the fossilised conifer resin gemologists call succinite, formed around 40 million years ago in the Baltic region — hand-set in solid 925 sterling silver. Because the stone is natural rather than pressed or dyed, every ring is one of a kind, with its own color and inclusions, and each ships with a certificate of authenticity. To check amber yourself, note that it is warm to the touch, floats in salt water, and is far lighter than glass.

en: Baltic amber, known to gemologists as succinite, is fossilised resin from ancient conifer forests that grew around the Baltic Sea some 40 million years ago. Over millennia the resin hardened, mineralised and was carried by rivers and seas into the deposits mined today. It is remarkably light, warm to the touch, and glows from within — qualities no glass or plastic imitation can match.
old: L'ambre de la Baltique, que les gemmologues nomment succinite, est une résine fossilisée issue d'anciennes forêts de conifères qui s'étendaient autour de la mer Baltique il y a quelque 40 millions d'années. Au fil des millénaires, la résine s'est durcie, minéralisée, puis a été charriée par les rivières et les mers jusqu'aux gisements exploités aujourd'hui. Remarquablement léger, chaud au toucher, il semble s'illuminer de l'intérieur — des qualités qu'aucune imitation en verre ou en plastique ne saurait égaler.

en: Butterscotch amber, sometimes called butter amber, is natural Baltic amber that is creamy and opaque rather than clear and translucent. It is the same fossilised conifer resin known as succinite that formed around 40 million years ago in the Baltic region, and its soft, milky warmth comes from countless microscopic air bubbles trapped in the resin. Where clear honey amber transmits light, these bubbles scatter it, producing a gentle, buttery glow, and the denser the bubbles the deeper the butterscotch tone. The look is soft, antique and quietly luxurious, which is why AMBERRA sets it by hand in 925 sterling silver for elegant everyday pieces.
old: L'ambre butterscotch, parfois appelé ambre beurre, est un ambre de la Baltique naturel, crémeux et opaque plutôt que limpide et translucide. Il s'agit de la même résine fossilisée de conifère, la succinite, formée il y a environ 40 millions d'années dans la région de la Baltique ; sa douce chaleur laiteuse naît d'innombrables bulles d'air microscopiques emprisonnées dans la résine. Là où l'ambre miel limpide laisse passer la lumière, ces bulles la diffusent et créent un éclat doux et beurré : plus elles sont denses, plus la teinte butterscotch s'approfondit. Il en résulte un aspect doux, ancien et d'un luxe discret. C'est pourquoi AMBERRA le sertit à la main dans l'argent sterling 925 pour des bijoux élégants à porter au quotidien.

en: For thousands of years amber traveled the ancient "Amber Road" from the Baltic coast to the Mediterranean, prized by Greeks, Romans and Egyptians who believed it carried the warmth and light of the sun. The Greek word for amber, elektron, gave us the word electricity — rub amber and it draws light objects to it, an effect the ancients thought magical.

Das griechische Wort für Bernstein, elektron, schenkte uns das Wort Elektrizität: Reibt man Bernstein, zieht er leichte Gegenstände an – eine Wirkung, die die Menschen der Antike für magisch hielten.

en: Cognac amber is a deeper brown-gold, warmer and darker than honey amber, which is lighter and more clearly golden. Both are genuine natural Baltic amber, the fossilised conifer resin known as succinite that formed around 40 million years ago in the Baltic region; the difference in tone comes from how each stone formed and oxidised over time. Cognac sits between honey and cherry, gradually deepening as its surface reacts with air, and each stone shows its own gradient of brown and gold. It is one of the most wearable amber tones, rich enough to feel luxurious yet neutral enough for everyday, set by hand in 925 sterling silver.
old: L'ambre cognac est d'un brun doré plus profond, plus chaud et plus foncé que l'ambre miel, plus clair et nettement doré. Tous deux sont des ambres de la Baltique naturels authentiques, la résine fossilisée de conifère appelée succinite, formée il y a environ 40 millions d'années dans la région de la Baltique ; leur différence de teinte tient à la manière dont chaque pierre s'est formée et oxydée au fil du temps. Le cognac se situe entre le miel et le cerise, et s'intensifie peu à peu à mesure que sa surface réagit à l'air ; chaque pierre révèle son propre dégradé de brun et d'or. C'est l'une des teintes d'ambre les plus faciles à porter, assez riche pour paraître luxueuse, assez neutre pour le quotidien, sertie à la main dans l'argent sterling 925.

en: Baltic amber, known to gemologists as succinite, is fossilised tree resin roughly 40 million years old, formed from ancient conifer forests that grew around the Baltic Sea and the wider Baltic region including Poland, Lithuania and Latvia. Over millions of years the resin hardened and mineralised into the warm, glowing stone used in jewelry today. It is prized for its rich color, its light weight, and the tiny natural inclusions of air, plant matter or occasionally insects that prove its origin. AMBERRA works only with authentic natural Baltic amber, never pressed, reconstituted or dyed substitutes, setting each stone by hand in 925 sterling silver.
old: Балтийский янтарь, известный геммологам как сукцинит, — это окаменевшая смола деревьев возрастом около 40 миллионов лет. Он образовался из древних хвойных лесов, росших вокруг Балтийского моря и по всему Балтийскому региону, включая Польшу, Литву и Латвию. За миллионы лет смола затвердела и минерализовалась, превратившись в тёплый, светящийся камень, который используется в ювелирных украшениях сегодня. Его ценят за насыщенный цвет, лёгкость и крошечные природные включения — пузырьки воздуха, частицы растений, а иногда и насекомых, — подтверждающие его происхождение. AMBERRA работает только с подлинным природным балтийским янтарём, никогда не используя прессованные, восстановленные или окрашенные заменители, и вручную закрепляет каждый камень в серебре 925 пробы.

en: Every AMBERRA piece uses genuine natural Baltic amber and ships with a certificate of authenticity, so authenticity is guaranteed with each order. You can also confirm real amber yourself using the simple tests jewelers rely on: genuine amber floats in salt water, feels warm to the touch rather than cold like glass, becomes electrostatic and attracts light objects when rubbed, and smells faintly of pine or resin when warmed. Real amber is also noticeably lighter than glass or plastic and usually contains natural bubbles or inclusions. Our journal explains these at-home tests in more detail if you would like to verify amber yourself.
old: В каждом украшении AMBERRA используется подлинный природный балтийский янтарь, и к каждому заказу прилагается сертификат подлинности — так подлинность гарантирована с каждой покупкой. Вы также можете проверить янтарь сами с помощью простых тестов, которыми пользуются ювелиры: настоящий янтарь держится на поверхности солёной воды, на ощупь тёплый, а не холодный, как стекло, при трении электризуется и притягивает лёгкие предметы, а при нагревании издаёт едва уловимый аромат хвои или смолы. Кроме того, настоящий янтарь заметно легче стекла или пластика и обычно содержит природные пузырьки или включения. Если вы хотите проверить янтарь самостоятельно, в нашем журнале эти домашние тесты описаны подробнее.

en: AMBERRA sets its Baltic amber primarily in solid 925 sterling silver, the international standard for fine jewelry at 92.5 percent pure silver, with selected pieces finished in 18k gold plating over sterling. en: The blue itself is not pigment — it is fluorescence. Trace aromatic hydrocarbons formed as the resin fossilised absorb ultraviolet light and re-emit it as a luminous blue, strongest in sunlight. Only a small fraction of mined Baltic amber shows this effect, which is why untreated blue stones sit among the most sought-after fossil resins on earth.

en: Butterscotch amber, sometimes called butter amber, is natural Baltic amber that is creamy and opaque rather than clear and translucent. It is the same fossilised conifer resin known as succinite that formed around 40 million years ago in the Baltic region, and its soft, milky warmth comes from countless microscopic air bubbles trapped in the resin. Where clear honey amber transmits light, these bubbles scatter it, producing a gentle, buttery glow, and the denser the bubbles the deeper the butterscotch tone. The look is soft, antique and quietly luxurious, which is why AMBERRA sets it by hand in 925 sterling silver for elegant everyday pieces.
old: Ирисковый янтарь, который иногда называют масляным, — это натуральный балтийский янтарь сливочного, непрозрачного оттенка, в отличие от прозрачного и светящегося. Это та же окаменевшая смола хвойных деревьев, сукцинит, сформировавшаяся около 40 миллионов лет назад в Балтийском регионе. Мягкое молочное тепло ему придают бесчисленные микроскопические пузырьки воздуха, заключённые в смоле. Прозрачный медовый янтарь пропускает свет, а эти пузырьки рассеивают его, рождая нежное, маслянистое сияние; чем плотнее пузырьки, тем глубже ирисковый тон. Его облик мягок, благороден и сдержанно роскошен, поэтому AMBERRA вручную оправляет его в серебро 925 пробы, создавая изысканные украшения на каждый день.

en: Cognac amber is a deeper brown-gold, warmer and darker than honey amber, which is lighter and more clearly golden. Both are genuine natural Baltic amber, the fossilised conifer resin known as succinite that formed around 40 million years ago in the Baltic region; the difference in tone comes from how each stone formed and oxidised over time. Cognac sits between honey and cherry, gradually deepening as its surface reacts with air, and each stone shows its own gradient of brown and gold. It is one of the most wearable amber tones, rich enough to feel luxurious yet neutral enough for everyday, set by hand in 925 sterling silver.

en: Bali jewelry is a tradition of handcrafted metalwork rooted in centuries of our artisan culture. These skills pass from parent to child, making every piece a living piece of cultural heritage.

en: Artisan jewelry is jewelry designed and made by skilled makers by hand, in small numbers, rather than mass-produced by machine in a factory. An artisan piece is shaped, set and finished individually, so each one carries small natural variations and the character of the person who made it. It usually uses genuine materials — at AMBERRA, natural Baltic amber and solid 925 sterling silver — rather than plated base metal or imitation stones. Buying artisan jewelry means owning something closer to a one-of-a-kind object than an identical unit, and it directly supports the makers keeping traditional handcraft alive. Every AMBERRA piece is handmade and ships with a certificate of authenticity.
old: Авторские украшения создаются и изготавливаются вручную опытными мастерами, небольшими партиями, а не выпускаются массово на фабричных станках. Каждое авторское изделие формуется, закрепляется и отделывается отдельно, поэтому несёт в себе небольшие естественные различия и характер своего создателя. Как правило, в нём используются подлинные материалы — в AMBERRA это натуральный балтийский янтарь и цельное серебро 925 пробы, — а не дешёвый металл с покрытием или имитация камней. Выбирая авторские украшения, вы получаете вещь, близкую к единственной в своём роде, а не одну из множества одинаковых, и напрямую поддерживаете мастеров, сохраняющих традиционное ремесло. Каждое изделие AMBERRA выполнено вручную и поставляется с сертификатом подлинности.

Выбирая авторские украшения, вы получаете вещь, близкую к единственной в своём роде, а не одну из множества одинаковых, и напрямую поддерживаете мастеров, сохраняющих традиционное ремесло. en: How is artisan jewelry different from mass-produced?
old: Чем авторские украшения отличаются от массового производства?
new: Чем авторские украшения отличаются от украшений массового производства?

en: Mass-produced jewelry is cast or stamped in large identical batches by machine, often in plated base metal with pressed or synthetic stones, and finished for speed. Artisan jewelry like AMBERRA is the opposite: each piece is made and inspected by a person, in solid 925 sterling silver with genuine natural Baltic amber, so the setting, polish and fit of the stone are judged by eye. That means better-set stones, real materials, and pieces that are repairable and age into heirlooms rather than being thrown away. It also means each item is genuinely one of a kind, because both natural amber and the human hand introduce variation no factory line reproduces.
old: Украшения массового производства отливаются или штампуются машинами большими одинаковыми партиями — часто из дешёвого металла с покрытием, с прессованными или синтетическими камнями — и отделываются в расчёте на скорость. Авторские украшения, такие как AMBERRA, — полная противоположность: каждое изделие создаёт и проверяет человек, из цельного серебра 925 пробы и подлинного натурального балтийского янтаря, а закрепку, полировку и посадку камня мастер оценивает на глаз. Это означает надёжно закреплённые камни, настоящие материалы и украшения, которые можно отремонтировать и которые со временем становятся семейными реликвиями, а не отправляются в мусор. Кроме того, каждое изделие поистине единственное в своём роде: и натуральный янтарь, и рука мастера привносят различия, которые не воспроизведёт ни одна фабричная линия.

en: Bali jewelry is a tradition of handcrafted metalwork rooted in centuries of our artisan culture. The island's silversmiths — concentrated in villages like Celuk, Bali, and Sukawati — are celebrated worldwide for three signature techniques: <0>filigree</0> (delicate twisted wire designs), <1>granulation</1> (tiny metal spheres fused to surfaces), and <2>jawan</2> (applied granulation in traditional patterns). These skills pass from parent to child, making every piece a living piece of cultural heritage.
old: Украшения с Бали — это традиция ручной обработки металла, уходящая корнями в многовековую культуру наших мастеров. Ювелиры острова, сосредоточенные в таких деревнях, как Челук, Бали и Сукавати, известны во всём мире тремя фирменными техниками: <0>филигрань</0> (тонкие узоры из витой проволоки), <1>грануляция</1> (крошечные металлические шарики, напаянные на поверхность) и <2>джаван</2> (накладная грануляция в традиционных орнаментах). Эти навыки передаются от родителей к детям, и каждое изделие становится живой частью культурного наследия.

That natural variation means no two pairs are exactly alike, from deep cherry and cognac to golden honey, green and rare blue amber. en: The proof is in the object. Look closely and you see the tiny asymmetries of hand-work — a bezel that hugs the exact shape of one irregular amber cabochon, a solder seam placed by judgement, a polish that follows the form. These are not defects; they are the signature of a maker, and they are impossible to mass-produce.
old: Der Beweis liegt im Schmuckstück selbst. Bei genauem Hinsehen erkennen Sie die feinen Asymmetrien der Handarbeit: eine Zarge, die sich exakt an die Form eines unregelmäßigen Bernstein-Cabochons schmiegt, eine nach Urteil gesetzte Lötnaht, eine Politur, die der Form folgt. Dies sind keine Mängel, sondern die Handschrift eines Meisters, und sie lassen sich nicht in Serie herstellen.
new: Der Beweis liegt im Schmuckstück selbst. Dies sind keine Mängel, sondern die Handschrift ihres Schöpfers, und sie lassen sich nicht in Serie herstellen.

en: Our artisans work in the old silversmithing techniques: filigree, where fine silver threads are twisted and soldered into lace; granulation, where tiny beads of silver are fused to the surface; and hand-cut bezels shaped to each stone. Every join is soldered by hand and every surface is filed and burnished rather than machine-buffed.
old: Unsere Kunsthandwerker arbeiten mit traditionellen Techniken der Silberschmiedekunst: Filigran, bei dem feine Silberfäden gedreht und zu Spitze verlötet werden; Granulation, bei der winzige Silberkügelchen auf die Oberfläche aufgeschmolzen werden; und von Hand geschnittene Zargen, die jedem Stein angepasst sind. Jede Verbindung wird von Hand gelötet, jede Oberfläche gefeilt und poliert statt maschinell geschliffen.
new: Unsere Kunsthandwerker arbeiten mit traditionellen Techniken der Silberschmiedekunst: Filigran, bei dem feine Silberfäden gedreht und zu spitzenartigem Geflecht verlötet werden; Granulation, bei der winzige Silberkügelchen auf die Oberfläche aufgeschmolzen werden; und von Hand geschnittene Zargen, die jedem Stein angepasst sind. Jede Verbindung wird von Hand gelötet, jede Oberfläche gefeilt und von Hand poliert statt maschinell geschliffen.

en: Across many cultures amber has been a symbol of the sun, warmth, light, and life. Because it forms from tree resin that captured sunlight and living matter millions of years ago, it became associated with preserved life, memory, and continuity. In folk tradition amber was also worn as a protective talisman, believed to carry the warmth and energy of the sun close to the body. Its glowing golden color reinforced these associations across the Baltic, Mediterranean, and beyond. For this reason amber has long been given as a meaningful gift and passed between generations, carrying the idea of enduring warmth and connection rather than mere decoration.

en: For thousands of years, amber has been treasured not only for its warm glow but for what it represents. This golden fossilized resin has been a symbol of the sun, a protective talisman, and a carrier of ancient stories carried along trade routes that spanned entire continents. This guide explores the meaning of Baltic amber — its history, its symbolism, the folklore and traditional beliefs woven around it, and what its many colors have come to represent.

Cette résine dorée et fossilisée a été tour à tour symbole du soleil, talisman protecteur et dépositaire d'histoires anciennes, transportées le long de routes commerciales qui traversaient des continents entiers. Ce guide explore la signification de l'ambre de la Baltique : son histoire, son symbolisme, le folklore et les croyances traditionnelles qui l'entourent, ainsi que le sens attaché à chacune de ses couleurs.

en: Baltic amber, known to scientists as <0>succinite</0>, is not a stone in the mineral sense at all. It is fossilized tree resin — the hardened sap of ancient coniferous forests that grew around the Baltic region roughly <1>40 million years ago</1>. Over vast stretches of time, this sticky resin was buried, compressed, and slowly transformed through fossilization into the warm, translucent material we know today.
old: L'ambre de la Baltique, que les scientifiques nomment <0>succinite</0>, n'est pas à proprement parler une pierre au sens minéral. C'est une résine d'arbre fossilisée : la sève durcie des forêts de conifères qui couvraient la région baltique il y a environ <1>40 millions d'années</1>. Au fil d'immenses périodes, cette résine collante a été enfouie, comprimée, puis lentement transformée par la fossilisation en la matière chaude et translucide que nous connaissons aujourd'hui.

Sur des périodes immenses, cette résine collante a été enfouie, comprimée, puis lentement transformée par la fossilisation en la matière chaude et translucide que nous connaissons aujourd'hui.

en: Because it is organic in origin, amber carries a warmth that mineral gemstones rarely possess. It is light in the hand, warm to the touch, and glows from within rather than simply reflecting light off its surface. This living quality is central to the meaning that cultures across the world have attached to it. If you want to see how the material varies in real pieces, our guide to <0>amber colors</0> shows the full spectrum.
old: D'origine organique, l'ambre possède une chaleur que les gemmes minérales offrent rarement. Léger dans la main, doux et tiède au toucher, il rayonne de l'intérieur au lieu de simplement refléter la lumière à sa surface. Cette qualité vivante est au cœur du sens que les cultures du monde entier lui ont prêté. Pour découvrir comment la matière varie d'une pièce à l'autre, notre guide des <0>couleurs de l'ambre</0> en présente toute la palette.

en: Because amber forms by capturing and preserving living matter, it also became a symbol of <0>memory, continuity, and the passage of time</0>. To hold amber is, in a poetic sense, to hold a preserved moment from deep antiquity. Many cultures treated it as a bridge between the living present and an ancient past, a material that quietly connected the wearer to something far larger than a single lifetime.
old: Parce qu'il se forme en capturant et en préservant la matière vivante, l'ambre est aussi devenu un symbole de <0>mémoire, de continuité et du passage du temps</0>. Tenir un morceau d'ambre, c'est, d'une certaine manière poétique, tenir un instant préservé depuis la plus haute Antiquité. De nombreuses cultures y voyaient un pont entre le présent vivant et un passé lointain, une matière qui reliait discrètement celui qui la portait à quelque chose de bien plus vaste qu'une seule vie.

en: Balinese jewelry refers to ornamental pieces — rings, earrings, pendants, bracelets and more — produced by craftspeople on the island of Bali, Indonesia, using techniques and aesthetic principles rooted in the island's Hindu-Dharma spiritual culture. While "Bali jewelry" is sometimes used loosely to describe any jewelry with a tropical or bohemian feel, authentic Balinese jewelry is defined by its origin and its craft: pieces made by hand, in Bali, by artisans trained in the island's silver and goldsmithing lineage.

en: The AMBERRA ring collection encompasses dozens of designs, but five styles consistently lead in both sales and collector interest. en: Ancient peoples across Europe and the Mediterranean prized amber for jewelry, amulets, and ornamental objects. It appeared in burial goods, was fashioned into beads and talismans, and was valued as a mark of status and meaning. Its rarity, its warmth, and its mysterious origin — this glowing material that washed up on distant beaches — made it deeply desirable long before its scientific nature was understood.

en: Across many cultures amber has been a symbol of the sun, warmth, light, and life. Because it forms from tree resin that captured sunlight and living matter millions of years ago, it became associated with preserved life, memory, and continuity. In folk tradition amber was also worn as a protective talisman, believed to carry the warmth and energy of the sun close to the body. Its glowing golden color reinforced these associations across the Baltic, Mediterranean, and beyond. For this reason amber has long been given as a meaningful gift and passed between generations, carrying the idea of enduring warmth and connection rather than mere decoration.

en: Bali jewelry has a dressing range that few other jewelry traditions can match. The same amber and silver pieces that look completely natural on a linen beach dress in the tropics can carry genuine authority at a formal dinner. This versatility is not accidental — it is a consequence of the craft itself. Handmade Balinese jewelry has a warmth of surface and a depth of material that synthetic or mass-produced pieces cannot replicate, and this warmth reads across contexts in a way that purely "fashion" jewelry does not. Whether you are building a daily signature look, experimenting with stacking and layering, or dressing for a special occasion, this guide will help you get the most from your AMBERRA collection.

en: Before discussing styling specifics, it helps to understand what makes Bali jewelry visually distinctive — because its styling logic flows from its aesthetic character. Balinese jewelry is organic in form and rich in surface texture. Where contemporary fine jewelry tends toward mathematical precision and smooth planes, genuine Balinese silverwork is characterised by the slight asymmetries of hand-forming, the dimensional complexity of granulation and repoussé, and the interplay of polished and oxidised (darkened) silver surfaces that create depth and visual drama. Against these silver surfaces, the warm glow of Baltic amber provides the piece's central focal energy.
old: Avant d'aborder les conseils de style, il est utile de comprendre ce qui rend les bijoux de Bali visuellement singuliers, car leur logique de style découle de leur caractère esthétique. Les bijoux balinais sont organiques dans leurs formes et riches en textures. Là où la haute joaillerie contemporaine tend vers la précision mathématique et les surfaces lisses, l'orfèvrerie balinaise authentique se caractérise par les légères asymétries du façonnage à la main, la complexité tridimensionnelle de la granulation et du repoussé, et le jeu entre argent poli et argent oxydé (noirci), qui crée profondeur et intensité visuelle. Sur ces surfaces d'argent, l'éclat chaleureux de l'ambre de la Baltique apporte à la pièce son énergie centrale.

en: Pendant layering — wearing multiple necklaces at varying lengths — is one of fashion's most enduring styling techniques, and Baltic amber pendants layer with particular effectiveness because of their visual weight and tonal warmth. The approach at AMBERRA is to offer pendants at chain lengths that are designed to work in combination: a shorter chain sits at the collarbone, a medium chain falls to mid-chest, and a longer version reaches the sternum. When worn together, the three amber points of light create a visual cascade from neck to chest that has real formal impact.
old: La superposition de pendentifs — porter plusieurs colliers à différentes longueurs — est l'une des techniques de stylisme les plus durables de la mode, et les pendentifs en ambre de la Baltique s'y prêtent avec une justesse particulière, grâce à leur présence visuelle et à la chaleur de leurs tons. L'approche d'AMBERRA consiste à proposer des pendentifs sur des longueurs de chaîne conçues pour s'associer : une chaîne courte se pose sur la clavicule, une chaîne moyenne tombe à mi-poitrine, et une version plus longue atteint le sternum. Portés ensemble, ces trois points de lumière ambrée dessinent une cascade visuelle du cou à la poitrine, d'une réelle élégance habillée.

en: The market is full of look-alikes. Some are honest substitutes clearly labelled as resin or reconstituted amber; others are sold as the real thing at real-amber prices. Learning to tell the difference protects both your money and your trust in what you wear. The tests below are the same principles gemologists rely on, simplified for home use. Use two or three together — no single test is proof on its own, but a piece that passes several with flying colors is almost certainly genuine amber.
old: Le marché regorge d'imitations. Certaines sont des substituts honnêtes, clairement présentés comme de la résine ou de l'ambre reconstitué. D'autres sont vendues pour de l'ambre véritable, au prix de l'ambre véritable. Savoir faire la différence protège à la fois votre argent et la confiance que vous accordez à ce que vous portez. en: Baltic amber, known scientifically as succinite, is fossilized resin from ancient coniferous forests that grew around the Baltic region roughly 40 million years ago. It is prized for its rich color range, natural inclusions, and long cultural history along the ancient Amber Road that linked the Baltic to the Mediterranean. Its age, warmth of color, and the folklore surrounding it have made Baltic amber one of the most storied natural materials used in jewelry. The Baltic region holds the world's largest and most famous deposits of this resin, and its succinic acid content is among the highest of any amber. Each piece is one of a kind, carrying tiny bubbles or fragments of an ancient forest.
old: Baltischer Bernstein, wissenschaftlich Succinit genannt, ist fossiles Harz aus urzeitlichen Nadelwäldern, die vor rund 40 Millionen Jahren im Ostseeraum wuchsen. Geschätzt wird er für sein reiches Farbspektrum, seine natürlichen Einschlüsse und seine lange Kulturgeschichte entlang der antiken Bernsteinstraße, die das Baltikum mit dem Mittelmeerraum verband. Sein Alter, die Wärme seiner Farben und die Legenden, die ihn umgeben, machen Baltischen Bernstein zu einem der geschichtsträchtigsten Naturmaterialien der Schmuckkunst. Der Ostseeraum birgt die größten und berühmtesten Vorkommen dieses Harzes weltweit, und sein Gehalt an Bernsteinsäure zählt zu den höchsten aller Bernsteinarten. Jedes Stück ist ein Unikat und birgt winzige Bläschen oder Fragmente eines urzeitlichen Waldes.

en: The making of a single AMBERRA ring involves between four and twelve hours of skilled manual work, depending on the complexity of the design. The process begins with the selection and preparation of 925 sterling silver sheet and wire. For bands featuring granulation, tiny silver spheres are formed by melting small wire lengths on a charcoal block — a process that requires practiced hand control to achieve consistent sphere sizes. The spheres are then placed in their designed positions on the band surface and fused using a copper-salt bonding process that joins silver to silver without visible solder.
old: Die Fertigung eines einzigen AMBERRA Rings erfordert je nach Komplexität des Designs zwischen vier und zwölf Stunden kunstfertiger Handarbeit. Für Ringschienen mit Granulation werden winzige Silberkügelchen geformt, indem kurze Drahtstücke auf einem Holzkohleblock geschmolzen werden – ein Vorgang, der eine geübte Hand erfordert, um gleichmäßige Kugelgrößen zu erzielen. Anschließend werden die Kügelchen an ihre vorgesehenen Positionen auf der Ringschiene gesetzt und mithilfe eines Kupfersalz-Verfahrens verschmolzen, das Silber mit Silber ohne sichtbares Lot verbindet.

en: Sterling silver naturally tarnishes over time through contact with air, moisture and sulphur compounds found in everyday environments. For AMBERRA rings, regular wear is actually the best prevention — the friction of daily contact buffs the high surfaces and keeps the silver bright. When tarnish does appear, a soft silver polishing cloth — used lightly on the silver surfaces only, never on the amber — will restore the metal's brilliance. Avoid immersing amber in ultrasonic cleaners or steam cleaners; these can cause fractures or surface crazing in the stone. Store rings individually in the provided pouch to prevent silver-on-silver scratching. For rings not worn regularly, a small piece of chalk in the storage pouch absorbs atmospheric moisture and significantly slows tarnish. With this minimal care, a well-made AMBERRA ring will remain in excellent condition for decades and improve in character with age as the amber develops its characteristic aged patina.

en: Fake amber is most often made from copal, plastic, or glass. Copal is young, immature resin that resembles amber but has not fully fossilized, so it is much softer and can be sold as amber by mistake or intent. Plastics such as bakelite, celluloid, and modern polyester resin are moulded to look like amber but feel different and behave differently in tests. Glass imitations are heavy and cold to the touch and do not build static. Pressed or reconstituted amber, made from melted amber fragments, is technically amber but far less valuable than a single natural piece.
old: L'ambre contrefait est le plus souvent fabriqué à partir de copal, de plastique ou de verre. Le copal est une résine jeune, encore immature, qui ressemble à l'ambre sans s'être entièrement fossilisée ; beaucoup plus tendre, il peut être vendu comme de l'ambre, par erreur ou à dessein. Les plastiques tels que la bakélite, le celluloïd ou la résine polyester moderne sont moulés pour imiter l'ambre, mais ils n'offrent pas le même toucher et réagissent différemment aux tests. Les imitations en verre sont lourdes, froides au toucher et ne se chargent pas d'électricité statique. L'ambre pressé ou reconstitué, obtenu à partir de fragments d'ambre fondus, est techniquement de l'ambre, mais il a bien moins de valeur qu'une pièce naturelle d'un seul tenant.

en: A very low price is one of the strongest warning signs of fake or reconstituted amber. Genuine natural Baltic amber is a fossilized material tens of millions of years old, cut and set by hand, so authentic pieces command a fair price. Mass-produced beads sold for a few dollars are usually plastic, copal, or pressed amber rather than a single natural stone. Price alone is not proof either way, but bargain amber that looks perfectly uniform, flawless, and identical across every bead deserves careful testing. Always buy from a seller who provides a certificate of authenticity confirming natural Baltic origin.

Les perles produites en série et vendues pour quelques dollars sont généralement en plastique, en copal ou en ambre pressé, et non taillées dans une pierre naturelle unique. Le prix ne constitue pas une preuve en soi, dans un sens comme dans l'autre, mais un ambre bradé, parfaitement uniforme, sans le moindre défaut et identique d'une perle à l'autre mérite d'être examiné avec soin. Achetez toujours auprès d'un vendeur qui fournit un certificat d'authenticité attestant l'origine baltique naturelle.

en: There are places in the world where the boundary between the material and the sacred is unusually thin. Bali is one of them. The island's Hindu-Dharma spiritual culture permeates daily life with a completeness rarely found elsewhere — offerings placed at dawn at every doorstep, ceremonies filling the streets with music, incense and color, temples in every corner of every rice field. It is no coincidence that Bali produces some of the world's most spiritually resonant jewelry. The objects made here carry an intention that begins before the first silver is melted: the silversmith works in a tradition that regards the making of beautiful things as an act of devotion. This guide explores what that means — for the pieces, for the materials, and for the person who chooses to wear them.
old: Il est des lieux au monde où la frontière entre le matériel et le sacré se fait singulièrement ténue. Bali est de ceux-là. La culture spirituelle hindoue-dharma de l'île imprègne la vie quotidienne avec une plénitude rarement observée ailleurs : offrandes déposées à l'aube sur chaque seuil, cérémonies emplissant les rues de musique, d'encens et de couleurs, temples nichés à chaque recoin des rizières. Ce n'est pas un hasard si Bali donne naissance à certains des bijoux les plus chargés de spiritualité au monde. Les objets façonnés ici portent une intention qui naît avant même que le premier fil d'argent ne soit fondu : l'orfèvre s'inscrit dans une tradition qui considère la création de belles choses comme un acte de dévotion. Ce guide explore ce que cela signifie — pour les pièces, pour les matières, et pour la personne qui choisit de les porter.

en: Sterling silver naturally tarnishes over time through contact with air, moisture and sulphur compounds found in everyday environments. For AMBERRA rings, regular wear is actually the best prevention — the friction of daily contact buffs the high surfaces and keeps the silver bright. When tarnish does appear, a soft silver polishing cloth — used lightly on the silver surfaces only, never on the amber — will restore the metal's brilliance. Avoid immersing amber in ultrasonic cleaners or steam cleaners; these can cause fractures or surface crazing in the stone. Store rings individually in the provided pouch to prevent silver-on-silver scratching. For rings not worn regularly, a small piece of chalk in the storage pouch absorbs atmospheric moisture and significantly slows tarnish. With this minimal care, a well-made AMBERRA ring will remain in excellent condition for decades and improve in character with age as the amber develops its characteristic aged patina.

Bei AMBERRA Ringen ist regelmäßiges Tragen tatsächlich die beste Vorbeugung: Die Reibung im täglichen Gebrauch poliert die erhabenen Flächen und hält das Silber strahlend. Zeigt sich dennoch Anlauf, stellt ein weiches Silberpoliertuch – sanft und ausschließlich auf den Silberflächen angewendet, niemals auf dem Bernstein – den Glanz des Metalls wieder her. Vermeiden Sie es, Bernstein in Ultraschall- oder Dampfreinigungsgeräte zu geben; diese können Risse oder feine Haarrisse an der Oberfläche des Steins verursachen. Bewahren Sie Ihre Ringe einzeln im mitgelieferten Beutel auf, um Kratzer durch Silber auf Silber zu vermeiden. Bei Ringen, die Sie nicht regelmäßig tragen, nimmt ein kleines Stück Kreide im Aufbewahrungsbeutel die Luftfeuchtigkeit auf und verlangsamt das Anlaufen deutlich. Set in silver with a Baltic amber center stone, the lotus pendant is one of AMBERRA's most enduringly beloved designs, combining visual elegance with layered spiritual meaning.

en: Bali jewelry has a dressing range that few other jewelry traditions can match. The same amber and silver pieces that look completely natural on a linen beach dress in the tropics can carry genuine authority at a formal dinner. This versatility is not accidental — it is a consequence of the craft itself. Handmade Balinese jewelry has a warmth of surface and a depth of material that synthetic or mass-produced pieces cannot replicate, and this warmth reads across contexts in a way that purely "fashion" jewelry does not. Whether you are building a daily signature look, experimenting with stacking and layering, or dressing for a special occasion, this guide will help you get the most from your AMBERRA collection.
old: Bali-Schmuck besitzt eine stilistische Bandbreite, mit der nur wenige andere Schmucktraditionen mithalten können. Dieselben Stücke aus Bernstein und Silber, die zu einem Strandkleid aus Leinen in den Tropen ganz natürlich wirken, verleihen auch einem festlichen Dinner echte Präsenz. Diese Vielseitigkeit ist kein Zufall – sie entspringt dem Handwerk selbst. Handgefertigter balinesischer Schmuck besitzt eine Wärme der Oberfläche und eine Tiefe des Materials, die synthetische oder in Serie gefertigte Stücke nicht nachahmen können, und diese Wärme entfaltet ihre Wirkung in jedem Kontext – anders als reiner „Mode“-Schmuck. Ob Sie einen persönlichen Signature-Look für jeden Tag entwickeln, mit Stacking und Layering experimentieren oder sich für einen besonderen Anlass kleiden: Dieser Guide hilft Ihnen, das Beste aus Ihrer AMBERRA-Kollektion herauszuholen.

en: The result is jewelry with a strong individual presence — pieces that want to be the jewel in the crown of an outfit, not blend into it. This understanding shapes the fundamental styling principle: <0>let the jewelry lead</0>. Build your outfit around your AMBERRA pieces rather than treating them as an afterthought, and the results will be consistently stronger. Amber's warm, earthy tones anchor naturally in organic fabric palettes — linen, silk, cotton, cashmere — and the handcrafted quality of the silver reads most powerfully against understated, quality clothing rather than competing pattern or embellishment.
old: Das Ergebnis ist Schmuck mit ausgeprägter Persönlichkeit – Stücke, die das Glanzlicht eines Outfits sein wollen, statt darin unterzugehen. Daraus ergibt sich das grundlegende Stylingprinzip: <0>Lassen Sie dem Schmuck die Hauptrolle</0>. Stellen Sie Ihr Outfit um Ihre AMBERRA-Stücke herum zusammen, statt sie als nachträglichen Einfall zu behandeln – das Ergebnis wird durchweg überzeugender sein. Die warmen, erdigen Töne des Bernsteins harmonieren ganz natürlich mit Farbpaletten aus Naturstoffen – Leinen, Seide, Baumwolle, Kaschmir –, und die handwerkliche Qualität des Silbers kommt am stärksten vor zurückhaltender, hochwertiger Kleidung zur Geltung statt neben konkurrierenden Mustern oder Verzierungen.

en: Pendant layering — wearing multiple necklaces at varying lengths — is one of fashion's most enduring styling techniques, and Baltic amber pendants layer with particular effectiveness because of their visual weight and tonal warmth. The approach at AMBERRA is to offer pendants at chain lengths that are designed to work in combination: a shorter chain sits at the collarbone, a medium chain falls to mid-chest, and a longer version reaches the sternum. When worn together, the three amber points of light create a visual cascade from neck to chest that has real formal impact.

The amber becomes the story. For maximalist layering, pair two or three AMBERRA pendants — ideally with amber stones in related but not identical tones — at varying lengths, and consider adding a fine plain chain at the shortest or longest position to create spacing and visual rhythm.

en: Before discussing styling specifics, it helps to understand what makes Bali jewelry visually distinctive — because its styling logic flows from its aesthetic character. Balinese jewelry is organic in form and rich in surface texture. Where contemporary fine jewelry tends toward mathematical precision and smooth planes, genuine Balinese silverwork is characterised by the slight asymmetries of hand-forming, the dimensional complexity of granulation and repoussé, and the interplay of polished and oxidised (darkened) silver surfaces that create depth and visual drama. Against these silver surfaces, the warm glow of Baltic amber provides the piece's central focal energy.
old: Прежде чем перейти к тонкостям стиля, важно понять, чем украшения Бали выделяются визуально, ведь логика их сочетания вытекает из их эстетического характера. Балийские украшения органичны по форме и богаты фактурой. Если современная ювелирная классика тяготеет к математической точности и гладким плоскостям, то подлинное балийское серебро отличают лёгкая асимметрия ручной формовки, объёмная сложность зерни и чеканки, а также игра полированных и оксидированных (затемнённых) поверхностей, создающая глубину и выразительность. На фоне серебра тёплое сияние балтийского янтаря становится смысловым центром изделия.

en: Baltic amber is the fossilized resin of ancient trees that grew along the shores of the Baltic Sea some 44 million years ago. Prized since the Neolithic period, it is one of the world's oldest traded luxury materials — ancient Roman merchants called it "the gold of the north." Its warm honey tones range from pale champagne to deep cognac and rare green, each piece unique in its inclusions, clarity and color depth.

Ценимый ещё с эпохи неолита, он входит в число древнейших предметов роскоши в мировой торговле: римские купцы называли его «золотом севера». Его тёплые медовые оттенки варьируются от светлого шампанского до глубокого коньячного и редкого зелёного, и каждый камень неповторим своими включениями, прозрачностью и глубиной цвета.

en: There are places in the world where the boundary between the material and the sacred is unusually thin. Bali is one of them. The island's Hindu-Dharma spiritual culture permeates daily life with a completeness rarely found elsewhere — offerings placed at dawn at every doorstep, ceremonies filling the streets with music, incense and color, temples in every corner of every rice field. It is no coincidence that Bali produces some of the world's most spiritually resonant jewelry. The objects made here carry an intention that begins before the first silver is melted: the silversmith works in a tradition that regards the making of beautiful things as an act of devotion. This guide explores what that means — for the pieces, for the materials, and for the person who chooses to wear them.
old: Есть на свете места, где граница между материальным и священным необычайно тонка. Бали — одно из них. Неслучайно именно на Бали создают одни из самых духовно наполненных украшений в мире. Предметы, рождённые здесь, несут намерение, которое возникает ещё до того, как будет расплавлено первое серебро: мастер-ювелир работает в традиции, где создание прекрасного считается актом служения. en: Under a <0>UV or blacklight</0>, genuine Baltic amber fluoresces — it typically glows a pale blue or milky blue-green, especially on an uncut surface. Copal shows a much weaker glow, and most plastics either stay dull or fluoresce a flat white. A small UV torch is inexpensive and makes this one of the more telling checks, though results vary with the amber's color and finish, so read it alongside the other tests rather than on its own.

en: Hold the piece to the light and look closely, ideally with a loupe or magnifier. Natural amber often contains <0>tiny bubbles, plant fragments, cracks, or subtle variations in color</0>. These small imperfections are a hallmark of the real thing. Imitations, by contrast, tend to look <1>too perfect</1> — flawlessly clear, uniformly colored, or dotted with suspiciously large, dramatic "insects" placed to impress. Perfectly identical beads across an entire strand are a warning sign of moulded plastic or pressed amber.
old: Halten Sie das Stück gegen das Licht und betrachten Sie es genau, idealerweise mit einer Lupe. Natürlicher Bernstein enthält häufig <0>winzige Bläschen, Pflanzenfragmente, Risse oder feine Farbnuancen</0>. Diese kleinen Unregelmäßigkeiten sind ein Kennzeichen des Echten. Imitationen wirken dagegen oft <1>zu perfekt</1> – makellos klar, gleichmäßig gefärbt oder mit verdächtig großen, spektakulären „Insekten“ versehen, die beeindrucken sollen. Vollkommen identische Perlen an einem ganzen Strang sind ein Warnsignal für gegossenen Kunststoff oder Pressbernstein.

en: This is the one <0>destructive test</0>, so use it only on raw material or where a tiny mark will not matter — never on a finished piece of jewelry. A needle heated and touched to the surface makes genuine amber release a faint <1>piney, resinous scent</1>. Copal smells sweeter and softens quickly. Plastic gives off a sharp, acrid chemical smell of burning synthetic. Because it leaves a mark, most people skip this test on jewelry and rely on the six non-destructive checks above.

Berührt man die Oberfläche mit einer erhitzten Nadel, verströmt echter Bernstein einen feinen <1>harzigen Duft, der an Kiefern erinnert</1>. Kopal riecht süßlicher und wird schnell weich. Kunststoff verströmt den scharfen, beißenden Geruch verbrannter Chemie. Da dieser Test eine Spur hinterlässt, verzichten die meisten bei Schmuck darauf und verlassen sich auf die sechs zerstörungsfreien Tests oben.

en: Yes. Genuine Baltic amber has a density close to that of saturated salt water, so it floats or hovers just below the surface while denser materials sink. To run the test, stir about two tablespoons of salt into a cup of warm water until no more dissolves, then gently drop the piece in. Amber and copal both float, while most plastics and all glass imitations sink to the bottom. The salt water test is one of the most reliable non-destructive checks, but pair it with the warmth and static tests, since copal floats too and needs further checks to distinguish from true amber.
old: Ja. Echter Baltischer Bernstein hat eine Dichte, die der von gesättigtem Salzwasser sehr nahe kommt; er schwimmt daher an der Oberfläche oder schwebt knapp darunter, während dichtere Materialien sinken. Für den Test rühren Sie etwa zwei Esslöffel Salz in eine Tasse warmes Wasser, bis sich nichts mehr löst, und legen das Stück dann behutsam hinein. Bernstein und Kopal schwimmen beide, während die meisten Kunststoffe und alle Glasimitate auf den Grund sinken. Der Salzwassertest gehört zu den zuverlässigsten zerstörungsfreien Prüfungen; kombinieren Sie ihn jedoch mit dem Wärme- und dem Statiktest, denn auch Kopal schwimmt und muss durch weitere Prüfungen von echtem Bernstein unterschieden werden.

en: To understand why Bali produces spiritual jewelry of a quality and authenticity unmatched elsewhere, you must understand the island's relationship with the sacred. Unlike societies where religion occupies a separate domain from everyday life, Balinese Hinduism is an integrated spiritual ecology. The divine is understood to inhabit all natural things — stones, trees, water, silver — and the act of shaping these materials with skill and intention is seen as participation in the divine creative process. A silversmith in Bali does not merely make a ring; in the Balinese understanding, they participate in the ongoing creation of a sacred object.
old: Um zu verstehen, warum auf Bali spiritueller Schmuck von einer Qualität und Authentizität entsteht, die anderswo unerreicht ist, muss man das Verhältnis der Insel zum Heiligen verstehen. Anders als in Gesellschaften, in denen die Religion einen vom Alltag getrennten Bereich einnimmt, ist der balinesische Hinduismus eine ganzheitliche spirituelle Ökologie. Nach diesem Verständnis wohnt das Göttliche in allen natürlichen Dingen – in Steinen, Bäumen, Wasser, Silber –, und diese Materialien mit Können und Intention zu formen, gilt als Teilhabe am göttlichen Schöpfungsprozess. Ein Silberschmied auf Bali fertigt nicht bloß einen Ring; nach balinesischem Verständnis wirkt er an der fortwährenden Erschaffung eines heiligen Objekts mit.

In jewelry, it appears in abstracted form: the characteristic wide eyes, pronounced brows and open mouth rendered in repoussé silver, often framing the central amber stone. The Kala's protective function makes it particularly valued in pieces intended as gifts for travel or new ventures.

en: Baltic amber is not a stone in the geological sense — it is fossilized plant resin, transformed over 44 million years of pressure and time into a material of extraordinary beauty and complexity. It is precisely this organic origin that gives Baltic amber its distinctive spiritual associations across cultures. Where minerals are shaped by geological force, amber is shaped by biology — by the living process of trees producing resin to heal their own wounds. This origin gives amber a connection to the natural world's healing intelligence that resonates deeply in traditions that regard nature as sacred.
old: Балтийский янтарь — не камень в геологическом смысле: это окаменевшая растительная смола, которая за 44 миллиона лет под действием давления и времени превратилась в материал необычайной красоты и сложности. Именно органическое происхождение придаёт балтийскому янтарю особые духовные ассоциации в самых разных культурах. Если минералы формируются геологическими силами, то янтарь создаёт биология — живой процесс, в котором деревья выделяют смолу, чтобы залечить собственные раны. en: Baltic amber has been considered a sacred material across many cultures for thousands of years. Its fossilized origin — ancient tree resin transformed over 44 million years — gives it an association with deep time, natural wisdom and protective energy. Known as the "stone of the sun" in Baltic and Slavic traditions, it has been used in healing and protective amulets for millennia.

Each piece is handcrafted by our artisans in 925 sterling silver and set with genuine Baltic amber.

en: AMBERRA amber pendants are available in a full spectrum of natural Baltic amber tones, including cherry, cognac, honey, green, butterscotch and rare blue amber, depending on the individual piece. Every color is natural to the stone rather than dyed or artificially treated, so each pendant is one of a kind, cut from genuine Baltic amber and finished by hand. en: Yes, all AMBERRA settings are solid 925 sterling silver, meaning 92.5 percent pure silver, the international standard for fine jewelry. Some pieces add 18k gold plating over sterling for a warmer look, but none use plated base metal beneath. Sterling silver alloys pure silver with a small amount of other metal for strength, since pure silver alone is too soft to hold a stone securely. Because our sterling is nickel-free, it is hypoallergenic and safe for sensitive skin. Every setting is hand-forged by our artisans, and each order includes a certificate of authenticity covering both the amber and the metal.

L'argent sterling allie l'argent pur à une petite part d'un autre métal qui le rend plus solide, car l'argent pur seul est trop tendre pour maintenir une pierre en toute sécurité. en: Where a diamond or sapphire is prized for hardness and sparkle, amber offers something different: warmth, color and a direct connection to the natural world. It is a fossil, not a cut crystal — light, glowing and alive with tiny inclusions. That makes an amber ring feel personal and organic rather than formal, a piece you wear for its character rather than its carat weight.
old: Если бриллиант или сапфир ценят за твёрдость и блеск, янтарь дарит иное: тепло, цвет и прямую связь с природой. Это окаменелость, а не ограненный кристалл — лёгкий, светящийся, оживлённый крошечными включениями. Поэтому кольцо с янтарём ощущается личным и природным, а не официальным: его носят ради характера, а не ради каратов.

en: Explore the complete AMBERRA collection of handcrafted Baltic amber jewelry — rings, earrings, pendants, bracelets and sterling silver chains. Every piece is cut from genuine Baltic amber (succinite), the fossilised conifer resin roughly 40 million years old from the Baltic region, and set by hand in 925 sterling silver in our atelier. Choose from natural amber colors including cherry, honey, cognac, green and rare blue, each stone one of a kind. Every order arrives with a certificate of authenticity and ships worldwide, free over $1,000.

en: Explore the complete AMBERRA collection of handcrafted Baltic amber jewelry — rings, earrings, pendants, bracelets and sterling silver chains. Every piece is cut from genuine Baltic amber (succinite), the fossilised conifer resin roughly 40 million years old from the Baltic region, and set by hand in 925 sterling silver in our atelier. Choose from natural amber colors including cherry, honey, cognac, green and rare blue, each stone one of a kind. Every order arrives with a certificate of authenticity and ships worldwide, free over $1,000.

en: Woven silver bracelets use fine-gauge sterling silver wire drawn through a traditional Balinese weaving form — a labor-intensive process that can take up to six hours per piece. Amber stones are set into the weave at regular intervals, appearing as warm points of color within the silver surface. Cast bracelets are made by pouring molten silver into hand-carved wax molds, then finishing the surface by hand with chisels and files. Bead bracelets string natural amber beads on a reinforced silk cord with a silver clasp — these are lighter in weight and more flexible in sizing.

Янтарные камни вплетаются через равные промежутки и проступают тёплыми акцентами цвета на серебряной поверхности. en: Our earring styles are organized into four families. Drop earrings feature one or more amber stones suspended below a silver post or hook — these range from 2cm to 8cm in length and include both delicate single-stone designs and elaborate multi-tier arrangements. Stud earrings are our most versatile style: a single amber cabochon set flush in a silver bezel, available in cognac, honey, cherry, and green amber. Hoop earrings integrate amber into a continuous silver curve. Chandelier earrings are AMBERRA's signature: wide, layered structures combining multiple amber stones with fine filigree silverwork.

en: Yes, all AMBERRA settings are solid 925 sterling silver, meaning 92.5 percent pure silver, the international standard for fine jewelry. Some pieces add 18k gold plating over sterling for a warmer look, but none use plated base metal beneath. Sterling silver alloys pure silver with a small amount of other metal for strength, since pure silver alone is too soft to hold a stone securely. Because our sterling is nickel-free, it is hypoallergenic and safe for sensitive skin. Every setting is hand-forged by our artisans, and each order includes a certificate of authenticity covering both the amber and the metal.

en: Sterling silver can darken slowly over time as it naturally reacts with air and moisture, forming a patina. This is normal and easily reversed: simply wipe the metal with a soft cloth and store your jewelry dry, ideally in a soft pouch with an anti-tarnish strip. Worn regularly, sterling silver actually tarnishes less, because the oils of your skin and the friction of wear help keep it bright. Because amber is a soft, organic stone, avoid dipping AMBERRA pieces in silver-cleaning solutions or using ultrasonic machines, which can dull or crack the amber. Polish the silver separately with a proper silver cloth.

en: Avoid perfume, heat and ultrasonic cleaners, since amber is a soft, organic stone that chemicals and vibration can damage. Wipe the ring gently with a soft cloth and store it apart from harder gemstones that could scratch it. Put the ring on last, after lotion and hairspray, and take it off before showering, swimming or sleeping. The 925 sterling silver setting darkens slowly with air; a soft silver cloth restores its shine. Cared for simply, an amber ring keeps its warm glow for decades.
old: Eviti profumi, fonti di calore e pulitori a ultrasuoni: l'ambra è una pietra organica e delicata, che le sostanze chimiche e le vibrazioni possono danneggiare. Pulisca l'anello con delicatezza usando un panno morbido e lo conservi separato dalle gemme più dure, che potrebbero graffiarlo. Indossi l'anello per ultimo, dopo creme e lacca, e lo tolga prima della doccia, di nuotare o di dormire. La montatura in argento sterling 925 si scurisce lentamente a contatto con l'aria; un panno morbido per argento ne ravviva la lucentezza. Con semplici attenzioni, un anello in ambra conserva il suo caldo bagliore per decenni.

en: The single biggest choice in an amber ring is color, and it is entirely natural to the stone. Cherry and cognac are the deepest, most saturated tones — dramatic on the hand and flattering as a formal or statement ring. Honey is the classic warm gold most people picture when they think of amber: versatile, timeless and easy to wear every day. Green and blue amber are the rarest, prized by collectors for how they shift under different light.
old: La elección más importante en un anillo de ámbar es el color, y es completamente natural de la piedra. El cereza y el coñac son los tonos más profundos y saturados: espectaculares en la mano y favorecedores en un anillo de gala o de impacto. El miel es el dorado cálido clásico que la mayoría imagina al pensar en el ámbar: versátil, atemporal y fácil de llevar a diario. El ámbar verde y el azul son los más escasos, apreciados por los coleccionistas por cómo cambian bajo distintas luces.

en: A gemstone ring is usually about the mineral — its cut, its clarity, its fire. An amber ring is different: amber is not a mined crystal but fossilised tree resin, warm and organic, that formed in ancient forests around 40 million years ago. Wearing one is closer to wearing a piece of deep time than a faceted stone, and it sits warm against the skin rather than cold like quartz or glass.

Un anello in ambra è diverso: l'ambra non è un cristallo estratto dalla terra, ma resina d'albero fossilizzata, calda e organica, formatasi in foreste antiche circa 40 milioni di anni fa. Indossarla significa portare con sé un frammento di tempo profondo più che una pietra sfaccettata, e sulla pelle resta calda, anziché fredda come il quarzo o il vetro.

en: Baltic amber, known to gemologists as succinite, is fossilised resin from ancient conifer forests that grew around the Baltic Sea some 40 million years ago. Over millennia the resin hardened, mineralised and was carried by rivers and seas into the deposits mined today. It is remarkably light, warm to the touch, and glows from within — qualities no glass or plastic imitation can match.
old: O âmbar báltico, que os gemólogos chamam de succinita, é a resina fossilizada de antigas florestas de coníferas que cresciam ao redor do Mar Báltico há cerca de 40 milhões de anos. Ao longo de milênios, a resina endureceu, mineralizou-se e foi levada por rios e mares até as jazidas exploradas hoje. É notavelmente leve, morno ao toque e brilha de dentro para fora — qualidades que nenhuma imitação em vidro ou plástico consegue igualar.

Ao longo de milênios, a resina endureceu, mineralizou-se e foi levada por rios e mares até as jazidas exploradas hoje. É notavelmente leve, agradavelmente quente ao toque e brilha de dentro para fora — qualidades que nenhuma imitação em vidro ou plástico consegue igualar.

en: Amber is organic and soft compared to hard gemstones, so a little care keeps it beautiful for a lifetime. Put your jewelry on last, after perfume, hairspray and lotion, and take it off before showering, swimming or sleeping. Wipe it with a soft, slightly damp cloth — never ultrasonic cleaners, solvents or hot water.
old: O âmbar é orgânico e macio em comparação às gemas duras, por isso um pouco de cuidado o mantém belo por toda a vida. Coloque suas joias por último, depois do perfume, do spray fixador e do hidratante, e retire-as antes do banho, de nadar ou de dormir. Limpe-as com um pano macio levemente umedecido — nunca use limpadores ultrassônicos, solventes ou água quente.

Depending on how the resin formed and how light passes through it, a stone can be deep cherry red, warm cognac, golden honey, cool green, rare blue, creamy butterscotch, or a mosaic of many tones at once. Every color in the AMBERRA collection is natural to the stone.

en: Amber is organic and soft compared to hard gemstones, so a little care keeps it beautiful for a lifetime. Put your jewelry on last, after perfume, hairspray and lotion, and take it off before showering, swimming or sleeping. Wipe it with a soft, slightly damp cloth — never ultrasonic cleaners, solvents or hot water.

Li pulisca con un panno morbido leggermente inumidito — mai pulitori a ultrasuoni, solventi o acqua calda.

en: Butterscotch amber, sometimes called butter amber, is natural Baltic amber that is creamy and opaque rather than clear and translucent. It is the same fossilised conifer resin known as succinite that formed around 40 million years ago in the Baltic region, and its soft, milky warmth comes from countless microscopic air bubbles trapped in the resin. Where clear honey amber transmits light, these bubbles scatter it, producing a gentle, buttery glow, and the denser the bubbles the deeper the butterscotch tone. The look is soft, antique and quietly luxurious, which is why AMBERRA sets it by hand in 925 sterling silver for elegant everyday pieces.
old: El ámbar butterscotch, a veces llamado ámbar mantequilla, es un ámbar báltico natural cremoso y opaco, en lugar de claro y translúcido. Es la misma resina fósil de conífera, conocida como succinita, que se formó hace unos 40 millones de años en la región del Báltico, y su suave calidez lechosa se debe a innumerables burbujas de aire microscópicas atrapadas en la resina. Mientras el ámbar miel transparente deja pasar la luz, estas burbujas la dispersan y crean un brillo suave y mantecoso: cuanto más densas son las burbujas, más profundo es el tono butterscotch. Su aspecto es suave, antiguo y discretamente lujoso, por eso AMBERRA lo engasta a mano en plata de ley 925 para crear piezas elegantes de uso diario.

en: Cognac amber is a deeper brown-gold, warmer and darker than honey amber, which is lighter and more clearly golden. Both are genuine natural Baltic amber, the fossilised conifer resin known as succinite that formed around 40 million years ago in the Baltic region; the difference in tone comes from how each stone formed and oxidised over time. Cognac sits between honey and cherry, gradually deepening as its surface reacts with air, and each stone shows its own gradient of brown and gold. It is one of the most wearable amber tones, rich enough to feel luxurious yet neutral enough for everyday, set by hand in 925 sterling silver.
old: L'ambra cognac ha un bruno-dorato più profondo, più calda e scura dell'ambra miele, che è più chiara e di un oro più limpido. Entrambe sono autentica ambra baltica naturale, la resina fossile di conifera nota come succinite, formatasi circa 40 milioni di anni fa nella regione baltica; la differenza di tonalità dipende da come ciascuna pietra si è formata e ossidata nel tempo. Il cognac si colloca tra il miele e il ciliegia, intensificandosi gradualmente man mano che la superficie reagisce con l'aria, e ogni pietra rivela la propria sfumatura di bruno e oro. È una delle tonalità d'ambra più facili da indossare, abbastanza ricca da trasmettere lusso e abbastanza neutra per ogni giorno, incastonata a mano in argento sterling 925.

en: AMBERRA is artisan jewelry in the true sense: a small independent studio, not a factory brand. Every design is drawn by hand, and every piece is made by the same makers who have worked silver and amber for years — not stamped out on a production line.

en: An artisan piece announces itself quietly. The stone sits in a setting cut to its own outline rather than a standard mould; the surface is finished by hand, so it holds a warmth that machine-buffing never quite gives; and the back is as considered as the front. These are the tells of a maker, not a mould.

en: We think jewelry should be judged the way a maker judges it — by how the parts meet, how the stone is held, how it feels in the hand. That is a standard you can only reach when a person, not a machine, has the final say on every piece.
old: Crediamo che un gioiello vada giudicato come lo giudica un artigiano: da come si uniscono le parti, da come è trattenuta la pietra, da come lo si sente nella mano. È uno standard che si raggiunge solo quando l'ultima parola su ogni pezzo spetta a una persona, non a una macchina.

en: Working small has a cost: we make in modest numbers and some pieces sell out. But it is the only way we know to keep quality honest and to keep the craft, and the makers, at the center of the brand rather than at the end of a supply chain.

en: Bali jewelry is a tradition of handcrafted metalwork rooted in centuries of our artisan culture. The island's silversmiths — concentrated in villages like Celuk, Bali, and Sukawati — are celebrated worldwide for three signature techniques: <0>filigree</0> (delicate twisted wire designs), <1>granulation</1> (tiny metal spheres fused to surfaces), and <2>jawan</2> (applied granulation in traditional patterns). These skills pass from parent to child, making every piece a living piece of cultural heritage.
old: La gioielleria balinese è una tradizione di lavorazione artigianale dei metalli, radicata in secoli della nostra cultura artigiana. Gli argentieri dell'isola, concentrati in villaggi come Celuk, Bali, e Sukawati, sono celebri in tutto il mondo per tre tecniche distintive: la <0>filigrana</0> (delicati motivi in filo ritorto), la <1>granulazione</1> (minuscole sfere di metallo fuse sulla superficie) e il <2>jawan</2> (granulazione applicata secondo motivi tradizionali). Questi saperi si tramandano di genitore in figlio e fanno di ogni creazione una testimonianza viva del patrimonio culturale.

en: For thousands of years, amber has been treasured not only for its warm glow but for what it represents. This golden fossilized resin has been a symbol of the sun, a protective talisman, and a carrier of ancient stories carried along trade routes that spanned entire continents. This guide explores the meaning of Baltic amber — its history, its symbolism, the folklore and traditional beliefs woven around it, and what its many colors have come to represent.

Questa guida esplora il significato dell'ambra baltica: la sua storia, il suo simbolismo, il folclore e le credenze tradizionali che la circondano, e ciò che i suoi molteplici colori sono giunti a rappresentare.

en: The Baltic region — encompassing the coasts of modern Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia, along with neighboring shores — holds the world's largest and most storied deposits of this resin. When ancient trees wept resin, they sometimes captured insects, plant fragments, and tiny bubbles of prehistoric air. These natural inclusions are part of what gives genuine Baltic amber its character and its almost mythic reputation as a keeper of preserved life. Each piece is a small window into a forest that vanished long before humankind existed.
old: La regione baltica, che comprende le coste delle odierne Polonia, Lituania e Lettonia insieme ai litorali vicini, custodisce i giacimenti di questa resina più vasti e ricchi di storia al mondo. Quando gli alberi antichi stillavano resina, talvolta imprigionavano insetti, frammenti vegetali e minuscole bolle d'aria preistorica. Queste inclusioni naturali contribuiscono a conferire all'autentica ambra baltica il suo carattere e la sua fama quasi mitica di custode della vita preservata. Ogni esemplare è una piccola finestra su una foresta scomparsa molto prima della comparsa dell'umanità.

en: The Baltic region — encompassing the coasts of modern Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia, along with neighboring shores — holds the world's largest and most storied deposits of this resin. When ancient trees wept resin, they sometimes captured insects, plant fragments, and tiny bubbles of prehistoric air. These natural inclusions are part of what gives genuine Baltic amber its character and its almost mythic reputation as a keeper of preserved life. Each piece is a small window into a forest that vanished long before humankind existed.
old: La región báltica, que abarca las costas de las actuales Polonia, Lituania y Letonia, junto con otras orillas vecinas, alberga los yacimientos de esta resina más extensos y legendarios del mundo. Cuando los árboles antiguos exudaban resina, a veces atrapaban insectos, fragmentos de plantas y diminutas burbujas de aire prehistórico. Estas inclusiones naturales forman parte de lo que confiere al ámbar báltico auténtico su carácter y su reputación casi mítica como guardián de vida preservada. Cada pieza es una pequeña ventana a un bosque que desapareció mucho antes de que existiera la humanidad.

en: The making of a single AMBERRA ring involves between four and twelve hours of skilled manual work, depending on the complexity of the design. The process begins with the selection and preparation of 925 sterling silver sheet and wire. For bands featuring granulation, tiny silver spheres are formed by melting small wire lengths on a charcoal block — a process that requires practiced hand control to achieve consistent sphere sizes. The spheres are then placed in their designed positions on the band surface and fused using a copper-salt bonding process that joins silver to silver without visible solder.

en: Sterling silver naturally tarnishes over time through contact with air, moisture and sulphur compounds found in everyday environments. For AMBERRA rings, regular wear is actually the best prevention — the friction of daily contact buffs the high surfaces and keeps the silver bright. When tarnish does appear, a soft silver polishing cloth — used lightly on the silver surfaces only, never on the amber — will restore the metal's brilliance. Avoid immersing amber in ultrasonic cleaners or steam cleaners; these can cause fractures or surface crazing in the stone. Store rings individually in the provided pouch to prevent silver-on-silver scratching. For rings not worn regularly, a small piece of chalk in the storage pouch absorbs atmospheric moisture and significantly slows tarnish. With this minimal care, a well-made AMBERRA ring will remain in excellent condition for decades and improve in character with age as the amber develops its characteristic aged patina.
old: A prata de lei escurece naturalmente com o tempo, pelo contato com o ar, a umidade e os compostos de enxofre presentes no dia a dia. Nos anéis AMBERRA, o uso frequente é, na verdade, a melhor prevenção: o atrito do contato diário pole as superfícies em relevo e mantém o brilho da prata. Quando o escurecimento surgir, uma flanela macia própria para prata, usada com leveza apenas sobre as superfícies de prata e nunca sobre o âmbar, devolverá o brilho ao metal. Evite mergulhar o âmbar em aparelhos de limpeza ultrassônica ou a vapor, que podem provocar fraturas ou microfissuras na superfície da pedra. Guarde cada anel separadamente na bolsinha que o acompanha, para evitar que a prata risque outras peças de prata. Para anéis usados com menos frequência, um pequeno pedaço de giz dentro da bolsinha absorve a umidade do ar e retarda consideravelmente o escurecimento. Com esses cuidados mínimos, um anel AMBERRA bem-feito se manterá em excelente estado por décadas e ganhará caráter com o tempo, à medida que o âmbar desenvolve sua característica pátina envelhecida.

en: Baltic amber, known scientifically as succinite, is fossilized resin from ancient coniferous forests that grew around the Baltic region roughly 40 million years ago. It is prized for its rich color range, natural inclusions, and long cultural history along the ancient Amber Road that linked the Baltic to the Mediterranean. Its age, warmth of color, and the folklore surrounding it have made Baltic amber one of the most storied natural materials used in jewelry. The Baltic region holds the world's largest and most famous deposits of this resin, and its succinic acid content is among the highest of any amber. Each piece is one of a kind, carrying tiny bubbles or fragments of an ancient forest.
old: El ámbar báltico, conocido científicamente como succinita, es resina fosilizada procedente de antiguos bosques de coníferas que crecieron en la región del Báltico hace unos 40 millones de años. Se aprecia por su rica gama de colores, sus inclusiones naturales y su larga historia cultural a lo largo de la antigua Ruta del Ámbar, que unía el Báltico con el Mediterráneo. Su antigüedad, la calidez de su color y el folclore que lo rodea han convertido al ámbar báltico en uno de los materiales naturales con más historia en joyería. La región del Báltico alberga los yacimientos de esta resina más grandes y célebres del mundo, y su contenido en ácido succínico es de los más altos de cualquier ámbar. Cada pieza es única y guarda diminutas burbujas o fragmentos de un bosque ancestral.

en: Baltic amber, known scientifically as succinite, is fossilized resin from ancient coniferous forests that grew around the Baltic region roughly 40 million years ago. It is prized for its rich color range, natural inclusions, and long cultural history along the ancient Amber Road that linked the Baltic to the Mediterranean. Its age, warmth of color, and the folklore surrounding it have made Baltic amber one of the most storied natural materials used in jewelry. The Baltic region holds the world's largest and most famous deposits of this resin, and its succinic acid content is among the highest of any amber. Each piece is one of a kind, carrying tiny bubbles or fragments of an ancient forest.

L'età, il calore dei suoi toni e il folclore che la circonda hanno reso l'ambra baltica uno dei materiali naturali più ricchi di storia mai impiegati in gioielleria. La regione baltica custodisce i giacimenti più vasti e celebri al mondo di questa resina, e il suo contenuto di acido succinico è tra i più elevati di qualsiasi ambra. Ogni pezzo è unico e racchiude minuscole bolle o frammenti di un'antica foresta.

en: Amber appears in many natural shades, and each carries its own associations. Honey and cognac amber evoke warmth, sunlight, and comfort. Cherry amber, deep and red-toned, suggests intensity and grounding. Green amber is linked to nature and renewal, while rarer blue amber is associated with mystery and depth. Butterscotch, mosaic, and raw amber each show the material in a different mood. These meanings are cultural and aesthetic rather than scientific, but they guide how many people choose a piece. The color of natural amber depends on how the resin formed and how light passes through it, so every shade is genuine to the stone rather than dyed. Many people simply choose the tone they feel most drawn to.
old: L'ambra si presenta in molte sfumature naturali, ciascuna con le proprie associazioni. L'ambra miele e cognac evoca calore, luce del sole e conforto. L'ambra ciliegia, profonda e dai riflessi rossi, suggerisce intensità e radicamento. L'ambra verde è legata alla natura e alla rinascita, mentre la più rara ambra blu è associata al mistero e alla profondità. Le varianti butterscotch, mosaico e grezza rivelano ciascuna un diverso carattere del materiale. Questi significati sono culturali ed estetici più che scientifici, ma orientano molte persone nella scelta di un gioiello. Il colore dell'ambra naturale dipende da come si è formata la resina e da come la luce la attraversa: ogni sfumatura appartiene dunque alla pietra stessa e non è frutto di tintura. Molti scelgono semplicemente il tono da cui si sentono più attratti.

en: The making of a single AMBERRA ring involves between four and twelve hours of skilled manual work, depending on the complexity of the design. The process begins with the selection and preparation of 925 sterling silver sheet and wire. For bands featuring granulation, tiny silver spheres are formed by melting small wire lengths on a charcoal block — a process that requires practiced hand control to achieve consistent sphere sizes. The spheres are then placed in their designed positions on the band surface and fused using a copper-salt bonding process that joins silver to silver without visible solder.
old: La creazione di un singolo anello AMBERRA richiede dalle quattro alle dodici ore di lavoro manuale qualificato, a seconda della complessità del disegno. Il processo ha inizio con la selezione e la preparazione di lastra e filo in argento sterling 925. Per le fasce decorate a granulazione, minuscole sfere d'argento vengono formate fondendo piccoli segmenti di filo su un blocco di carbone, un'operazione che richiede grande padronanza manuale per ottenere sfere di dimensioni uniformi. Le sfere vengono poi disposte nelle posizioni previste sulla superficie della fascia e fuse mediante un procedimento ai sali di rame, che unisce argento ad argento senza saldature visibili.

en: For ring bands featuring repoussé work, the sheet silver is worked from behind using steel punches against a pitch bowl — a hemispherical vessel of pitch that holds the metal firmly while allowing it to flex under pressure. The result is a three-dimensional relief that emerges from the band surface with extraordinary definition. The stone setting is crafted separately and soldered into the band after all decorative work is complete. AMBERRA's amber stones are set last, after all silverwork is finished, polished and inspected — protecting the amber from the heat and chemicals of the silversmithing process.

Ne nasce un rilievo tridimensionale che emerge dalla superficie della fascia con straordinaria nitidezza.
